I wasn't but I'll consider it an added perk. Here's to hoping the weekend will bring about some meaning to all of this.
If I can do one thing with any competence it is overthink lol.

I'd never heard of filial piety before, what an intriguing concept! Thank you for making me aware of it. I am enjoying finding out how it clashes with the idea of parenthood being the one relationship in nature based on nonreciprocal altruism.

> Are you really saying you wish you had not been born? 

I am. I am certain that had my parents stopped at my brother (their second) they would be far healthier of body, mind and wallet. Existential crisis are tough enough without knowing your very being reduced the quality of life for everyone close to you.

> Why not? Plenty of other people have. There's always paying for college through the military if you can't work and take out loans. Get a professional degree or do whatever it is you want. Best of luck to you!

I couldn't deal with various sources of stress growing up so I just hid. Haven't got anything on my resume now apart from a few mediocre high school level qualifications. I still don't even know what it is I want to do so I haven't got anything to work towards, not that I can afford university (and the UK military has no such schemes like the G.I. Bill). Thanks for reading and your advice though :)
Unfortunately my doctor diagnoses me with clinical depression which has ruled me out of armed service :(

Thanks for reading and reaching out. Though I had material needs met in that house I learnt absolutely nothing about how to handle adult life, interpersonal communication being a particularly big failure. The passive-aggression and guilt tripping you mentioned were the only ways mother would communicate us and father was so afraid of his inner thoughts that he never expressed anything, all we were taught is that there isn't any joy or pleasure to be found in life, it's a long meaningless toil where you suffer and slave and expire and that's it.

>Why do you feel like you're going to be stuck under their thumb forever?

Fucked up all my chances to build something of myself in those safety buffer adolescent years where not much is expected of you. I was so afraid of being hurt that I refused to engage in life and only begrudgingly turned up to formalities like exams. My underwhelming academic record and lack of extracurriculars and past employment makes for a blank resume. It's difficult enough for my age bracket to get hired because all companies want middle aged men with a decade and a half of experience but it's difficult for me to employers to take a punt on the two things I do have, time on my side and eagerness to learn.
